brief: TS Lombard argues current tech valuations assume an earnings share tech cannot sustain. For valuations to hold, revenue share must broaden beyond the tech complex, which energy costs and rate headwinds complicate. Staying risk-on requires profit broadening, which the firm believes is underway, arguing for rotation into the rest of the economy. If broadening instead stalls, the rest of the economy cannot afford tech and markets go risk-off, with bonds benefiting. Alternatively, weak links in the tech financing chain could pop under higher rates, triggering risk-off even if the macro improves. The firm prefers non-US sovereign debt over US Treasuries, since the rise in UST yields reflects domestic inflation more than the energy shock. It expects quarterly Fed hikes, citing bottoming low-income wage growth and inflation stuck below 2 percent, though it says the hawkish call is close to priced and Fed commentary is walking it back. Dropped hedging ratios leave the dollar exposed to a negative post-hedging shock if another US-centric shock hits. More air coming out of tech now, it argues, raises the odds of a sustained expansion and productivity gains, while letting leverage keep building raises the odds of a bigger, recession-causing unwind within one to two years.
